metadata.note: Match each of the 3 'R' environmental terms to its definition. 3 slots × 1m each. Word bank: 5 definition phrases (3 correct + 2 distractors). Definitions are phrased as actions: Reduce=use less, Reuse=use again without processing, Recycle=convert waste into new products.

question.name: CSEC Bio Jan 2024 Q3b — Match Reduce, Reuse, Recycle to Definitions
question.text:
Match each term to its correct definition by dragging the appropriate phrase into each blank:

TermDefinition
Reduce[[1]]
Reuse[[2]]
Recycle[[3]]
question.general_feedback:
The Three R's:

  • Reduce: Decrease the amount of waste produced by using fewer resources (e.g. buying only what you need, using less packaging)
  • Reuse: Use an item more than once in its original form without reprocessing (e.g. refilling a water bottle, donating old clothes)
  • Recycle: Convert waste materials into new products through processing (e.g. melting glass bottles into new glass, shredding paper into new paper pulp)

groups.label: Definition of Reduce
groups.diagnostic_hint: Reduce means to decrease the amount of waste produced by consuming fewer resources in the first place — prevention is better than cure.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 5 tokens for 3 slots; 3 correct + 2 distractors. 'Dispose of waste in a landfill' — common misconception; landfill is NOT one of the 3 Rs. 'Burn waste to generate energy' — this is incineration/waste-to-energy, sometimes confused with 'recycle'; it is NOT recycling since original material is not reformed into a new product of the same type.
